cues.text: Sunlight is white.
Space is black.
So why is the sky blue?
The answer is hiding inside every sunbeam.
And it also explains why sunsets turn red.
Sunlight looks white, but it is really every colour of the rainbow, travelling together.
Each colour is a wave.
Red waves are long and lazy.
Blue waves are short and choppy.
On its way down, sunlight crashes into the air itself.
Air is made of molecules, far smaller than the waves.
These tiny molecules bounce short blue waves around much more than long red ones.
About four times more.
So blue light gets scattered across the whole sky.
Wherever you look, some of that bounced blue is heading for your eyes.
The sky is not painted blue.
It is glowing blue.
At sunset, sunlight takes a much longer path through the air.
Most of the blue is scattered away before it reaches you.
What is left is orange and red.
So the sky is blue because air scatters blue light the most.
And a red sunset is the same trick, seen from the side.
